description: The bounds and text rules of the user bug report, as DATA, so the JavaScript reference implementation in ../src/bugReport.mjs and AUB's Go re-validation of a server-route submission apply the same rules rather than two sincere transcriptions. Since 1.1 it is also the ONE source of the report's GitHub classification: the application, report-type and area labels, which areas each application offers, the closed incident-to-area mapping, the per-type field headings and the bounded acceptance of the previous document version. A report is PUBLISHED on a public GitHub repository, so every rule here is a publication rule.

notes: The initial area of an incident-triggered report. It reads only the incident's typed fields — never prose. Order: an exact `by_subsystem` entry for the reporting application, else the exact `by_code` entry, else `other`; an area the reporting application does not offer becomes `other`. The user can change the suggestion before preview.
`by_code` has one entry for EVERY code in incident-codes.json; test/bug-report.test.mjs fails when the taxonomy gains a code this table does not map.

previous_schemas.note: A server may still accept a previewed 1.0 document until `accepted_until` (clients built before 1.1). It is labelled with its application, `report_type` and `area` from this entry. After that instant it is refused. Clients never emit it.

notes: The exact labels auto-pigeon/bug-reports must carry, with deterministic colours and descriptions. `Already tracked elsewhere` is the only manually applied label; there are no workflow, triage, priority or severity labels. Open/closed is the workflow state.

labels.name: Feature request
labels.description: A request for new or changed behaviour

labels.name: Already tracked elsewhere
labels.description: Closed because another issue is the canonical one

notes: Applied to every free-text field, in this order: lone UTF-16 surrogates become U+FFFD; CR LF, CR, U+2028 and U+2029 become LF; every code point in `removed_ranges` is deleted; a single-line field turns runs of LF/TAB into one space and runs of spaces into one; the central redaction value patterns run; trailing spaces/tabs are removed from every line; three or more LFs become two; leading and trailing space, TAB and LF are trimmed; and the result is cut to the field's limit in CODE POINTS, the last kept code point replaced by U+2026 when anything was cut.

Invisible and direction-changing characters are removed BEFORE redaction, so a zero-width joiner cannot split a token into two halves no pattern recognises, and before the public preview, so a right-to-left override cannot make the text a user approved read differently on GitHub.
Trim is deliberately only space, TAB and LF — not each language's own idea of whitespace, which differs between JavaScript and Go.

Every rule is idempotent: sanitising a sanitised value returns it unchanged. That is what lets a server refuse a submission whose text is not already canonical instead of silently publishing something the user did not preview.
